question: Section 2(12) of The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 defines a child as 'a person who has not completed ___________ years of age'.
solution:
The correct answer is __**18.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 was enacted to provide for the care, protection, and rehabilitation of children who conflict with the law and children in need of care and protection.
 
• **Section 2(12) **of The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 **defines a child as 'a person who has not completed 18 years of age**
 
 
• This means that any person who is **under the age of 18 is considered a child** under this act.
 
 
 
• The term "juvenile" is used to refer to a young person who is not yet an adult and is considered to be under the age of majority.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• An important provision of the amended Act is that it provides for minors in the age group 16 16–18 years to be treated as adults in the case of heinous crimes.
 
• It also gives definitions for petty, serious, and heinous crimes by children.
 
 
• A heinous offense attracts a maximum punishment of 7 years imprisonment under any existing law.
 
• A serious offense attracts imprisonment of 3–7 years.
 
• A petty offense attracts a maximum of 3 years of imprisonment.
 
 
 
• The Act gives more clarity on the functions and powers of the Juvenile Justice Board and the Child Welfare Commission.
